name: clear-project
description: A well-specified single-organisation brief. The analyst should capture its requirements with brief evidence, avoid unnecessary blocking questions, and may declare readiness.

configuration.name: Hourly
configuration.description: Internal timesheet web app for our 20-person design agency (one organisation). Employees log hours per client project each week, managers approve timesheets, and finance exports approved hours as CSV each month.

requirements.custom:
Email and password accounts are enough; no single sign-on.
Hours are rounded to 15 minutes.

context.goal: Track agency staff hours per client project, approve them weekly, and export them monthly for finance.
context.scope: Timesheet entry, manager approval, CSV export, and an admin dashboard for projects and users.

personas.name: Employee
personas.description: Logs hours per client project each week.

operations.statement: Employees log hours per client project for each week.
acceptance_criteria: An employee enters hours against two projects for a week and sees the weekly total.

operations.statement: Managers approve or return submitted timesheets.
acceptance_criteria: A manager approves one timesheet and returns another with a comment; the employee sees both outcomes.

operations.statement: Finance exports approved hours for a month as CSV.
acceptance_criteria: The export for a month contains exactly the approved entries, one row per employee, project, and day.

operations.statement: Users sign in with email and password.
acceptance_criteria: A user signs in with email and password; wrong passwords are rejected.

operations.statement: Logged hours are rounded to 15-minute increments.
acceptance_criteria: An entry of 1 h 07 min is stored and shown as 1 h 00 min; 1 h 08 min becomes 1 h 15 min.

operations.statement: Administrators manage users, roles, and client projects in an admin dashboard.
acceptance_criteria: An administrator adds a project and assigns a manager role to a user.

questions.prompt: Should rounding go to the nearest 15 minutes or always up?

assumptions.statement: Rounding is to the nearest 15 minutes until confirmed.

decisions: The brief settles the core scope, so no blocking questions were needed.
